facility_name: NSIA-LUTH Cancer Centre (now Medserve-LUTH Cancer Centre), Lagos University Teaching Hospital
evidence_note: A 2024 survey of Nigerian radiotherapy centres (data as of June 2023) reports the PPP centre treating with three LINACs. "has commenced services with three LINACs capable of delivering modern techniques such as intensity-modulated RT"

facility_name: NSIA-LUTH Cancer Centre (now Medserve-LUTH Cancer Centre), Lagos University Teaching Hospital
evidence_note: NSIA project page (undated; figure stated as of February 2024) gives cumulative unique patients treated since the centre began in May 2019. Page also lists 2 VitalBeam LINACs, 1 Halcyon and 1 GammaMed brachytherapy unit. "Provision of cancer treatment services to 9,410 unique patients as of February 2024"

facility_name: NSIA-LUTH Cancer Centre (now Medserve-LUTH Cancer Centre), Lagos University Teaching Hospital
evidence_note: Vendor (Radformation) case-study blog on the centre gives staff numbers and about 1,600 patients a year. Not independent; treat as news. "10 Clinical and Radiation Oncologists, 9 Medical Physicists, and 16 Radiation Therapists"

IAEA/WHO/IARC imPACT Review (mission 14-24 Oct 2024) says PPP arrangements at cancer centres in Enugu, Sokoto, Ebonyi and Lagos raised machine uptime above 95%; the Lagos facility is not named in the text. "These partnerships have increased the radiotherapy machine uptime to more than 95% in all four sites"

Survey of nine centres (data May 2020-April 2021), Table 2 marks Eko Hospital cobalt-60 as A (1)+, where + means in active use; Eko averaged 65 patients a month. "+: functional; −: not functional (an equipment is said to be functional if it’s in active use)"
Table 1 of a 2024 study (as of June 2023) lists one cobalt-60 at Eko Hospital with no "not operational" flag; the table does not otherwise state working status. "Eko Hospital 1 NA NA"
Table 1 of a 2024 study (as of June 2023) lists one LINAC at this private Lagos centre; working status not stated. "Marcelle Ruth Cancer Centre NA 1 NA"

Study of the eight government-funded centres (2021 data) says UCH had only an old, unused cobalt-60 and no functional teletherapy; no specific cause given for UCH. "Two centers, UCH and ABUTH, have old unused cobalt-60 teletherapy machines."

CONFLICTS with the row above: a survey with data May 2020-April 2021 marks UCH cobalt-60 as A (1)+ (functional = in active use); UCH saw about 65 patients a month. "UCH Ibadan attended to 65 patients on average per month"
Table 1 of a 2024 study (as of June 2023) lists one cobalt-60 at UCH flagged "a", defined in the footnote as not operational. "a Not operational."

imPACT Review: Ibadan was one of three centres whose radiotherapy service was not functional during the October 2024 mission; no cause given for Ibadan. "Three centres (Ibadan, Maiduguri and Zaria) that previously had radiotherapy were not functional at the time of the in-country mission."

UCH announced a partnership to install a LINAC; the shielded bunker to house it is still being built, so it is not yet treating patients. "Work on the specialised bunker required to house the equipment is ongoing."

Survey (data May 2020-April 2021) Table 2 counts 9 radiation oncologists at UCH, the most of the nine centres surveyed. "Radiation oncologist | 2 | — | 2 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 9 | 3 | 3 | 28" (columns: ABUTH, Eko, FTH Gombe, LUTH, NHA, UBTH, UCH, UNTH, UDUTH, Total)

facility_name: University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital, Ituku-Ozalla, Enugu
evidence_note: Study of government-funded centres (2021 data) lists UNTH among the three centres with a functional LINAC. "Only three (60%) of the five centers have functional LINACs, namely UNTH, NHA, and NSIA-LUTH."

facility_name: University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital, Ituku-Ozalla, Enugu
evidence_note: LINAC logbook study (2011-2018): the Enugu LINAC was down 54.7% of the time; vandalism and a fire delayed first treatment, Nigerian centres had no parts or service contract, and Enugu ran solely on generators. "the Nigeria centres do not have either a parts or service contract"

facility_name: University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital, Ituku-Ozalla, Enugu
evidence_note: A 2021 study reports UNTH used a PPP to buy a vendor service contract for its government-bought machine because public maintenance funding was unreliable. "University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital in Enugu established a PPP to purchase a vendor service contract for its government-acquired megavoltage unit"

facility_name: University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital, Ituku-Ozalla, Enugu
evidence_note: The Health Minister commissioned an additional LINAC and oncology upgrade at UNTH, with NSIA and Medserve as partners; commissioning does not confirm treatment use. "commissioning of an additional Linear Accelerator and Oncology Infrastructure Upgrade"

facility_name: University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital, Ituku-Ozalla, Enugu
evidence_note: Survey (data May 2020-April 2021) Table 2 counts 3 radiation oncologists and 7 medical physicists at UNTH. "Radiation oncologist | 2 | — | 2 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 9 | 3 | 3 | 28" (UNTH is the 8th column)

imPACT Review lists Ebonyi among the eight states with functional external-beam machines and among the four PPP sites with uptime above 95%; the facility is not named. "15 functional external beam machines (13 linear accelerators and 2 cobalt machines), distributed across eight states (Lagos, Enugu, Ebonyi, Cross River, Bono, Abuja, Kano and Sokoto)"

imPACT Review lists Cross River among the eight states with at least one functional external-beam machine at the October 2024 mission; the facility is not named. "distributed across eight states (Lagos, Enugu, Ebonyi, Cross River, Bono, Abuja, Kano and Sokoto)"

facility_name: Asi Ukpo Comprehensive Cancer Centre, Calabar
evidence_note: Table 1 of a 2024 study (as of June 2023) lists one LINAC at Asi Ukpo, the only South South centre with a LINAC in that table; working status not stated. "Asi Ukpo Comprehensive Cancer Centre NA 1 NA"

facility_name: Asi Ukpo Comprehensive Cancer Centre, Calabar
evidence_note: Nuclear regulator NNRA did a pre-authorisation inspection (14-15 March 2022; page undated) of a centre built for LINAC and HDR brachytherapy; commissioning/operating licences were still pending. "AUCCC is a Radiotherapy facility designed and constructed for an External Beam Radiotherapy (EBRT) with Linear Accelerator, and High Dose Rate (HDR) Brachytherapy."

Study of government-funded centres (2021 data): UBTH has a LINAC but no functional teletherapy; it does have a functional HDR brachytherapy unit. No UBTH-specific cause given. "Only three (60%) of the five centers have functional LINACs, namely UNTH, NHA, and NSIA-LUTH."

Survey (data May 2020-April 2021) Table 2 marks the UBTH LINAC as A (1)−, i.e. not in active use; cause not stated. "+: functional; −: not functional (an equipment is said to be functional if it’s in active use)"

LINAC logbook study (2013-2018 for Benin): 14.2% downtime; the Benin centre ran solely on generators because of grid power cuts, and had no parts or service contract. "The Benin, Enugu, Lagos and Sokoto centres are solely powered by generators to circumvent the frequent power cuts"

UBTH Chief Medical Director (31 Aug 2026) says the federal oncology centre (commissioned July 2025) is fully operational with a LINAC and CT simulator. "We have Linear Accelerator (LINAC) machine, 16-slice CT where we simulate the patient's lesion."

Table 1 of a 2024 study (as of June 2023) lists one cobalt-60 at this private Owerri centre, the only South East centre besides UNTH; working status not stated. "American Cancer Hospital, Owerri 1 NA NA"

facility_name: Dr. Peter Odili Cancer/Cardiovascular Diagnostic and Treatment Centre, Port Harcourt
evidence_note: Rivers State-owned centre (reported cost N26bn) opened to the public with radiotherapy and brachytherapy units; machine type, count and working status not given. "three theatres, a catheterisation laboratory, a radiotherapy unit, a brachytherapy unit and a nuclear medicine unit"
